deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 154, 1983-84). Grothendieck is building, purely combinatorially, a cell complex, and ultimately a closed surface, whose cells come from 'relative positions'. These are the combinatorial types of a pseudo-line D_i placed relative to a fixed system of pseudo-lines Sigma. The next page writes L = D_i + Sigma and works with the system (X, Sigma \ {D_i}). The generic positions are joined by 'arcs of transition' of two kinds. 'Specialization' arcs pass to a more degenerate position, e.g. D_i moving through a crossing of Sigma (a 'critical' position). 'Generalization' arcs go the other way. The previous page fixes the gluing isomorphisms (the 'isomorphismes de transport', taken opposite to the tautological one, i.e. the symmetry exchanging s and t). With that choice all 2-faces of the complex are of order 4. These faces are dual to the cycles closed off by the 'cas d'inertie'.

This page analyses such a square face. Its sides come from arcs of transition, and each side has a type:
- one 'specialization' side (both arcs ending there are specializations);
- one 'generalization' side;
- two 'mixed' sides.
Going round the square from the specialization side, the corners read, in cyclic order: spec→spec, gen→spec, gen→gen, spec→gen (traversed in one direction or the other).

Hence the 2-cells are in bijection with pairs (L, a). Here L is a relative position and a is an incidence (or 'inertia') arc of specialization type. Equivalently, a can be taken of generalization type, since the two kinds of pairs correspond 1-1.

Grothendieck prefers the generalization description. It amounts to listing:
(a) the pairs (S,L): closed critical digons of Sigma together with the relative positions leading to them;
(b) for each such datum, whether there is a contractibility arc with a 'cotriangle' above it, and choosing it (several may exist a priori).
He notes that the description is especially pleasant in the very special case where each digon gives a unique relative position.

The right-hand figure is a disk (yellow boundary) with four crossing orange pseudo-chords. The boundary arcs between endpoints are labelled 1-4 with arrows. It illustrates such a digon/cotriangle configuration, or the circular order of the transitions.

Last paragraph: the cellular surface is still incomplete. The 'hypercritical' relative positions (more degenerate, e.g. passing through several vertices or a multiple point) were omitted from the gluing. So were the specialization and generalization arcs to and from them. Hence free boundary circles remain, and these must be capped by further polygonal disks. The next page treats them as free edges (fixed by tau) of a graph Gamma = (S, A, sigma, tau): first a compact surface with boundary is formed, then its holes are plugged along the 'exceptional specialization' arcs.

Modern reading: this is a combinatorial construction of the 'space of one-element extensions' of a rank-3 oriented matroid / pseudoline arrangement as a regular cell complex. Squares correspond to commuting independent moves. Larger polygons correspond to higher-multiplicity degenerations, as in the 2-cells of the higher Bruhat / Manin–Schechtman complexes. The evident target is that this extension space is a surface (the projective plane, or a sphere in the affine/oriented setting).
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The argument is a sketch: the claim that every face is a square presupposes the convention for the transport isomorphisms fixed on the previous page.

Item (b) of the face description is left incomplete. The existence and uniqueness of the 'arc de contractibilité ... cotriangle' is asserted only 'a priori', with the possibility of several choices left open.
The surface is admitted to be incomplete (hypercritical positions are missing), so no global statement is proved on this page.

ideas.what: Cell complex whose vertices and edges are relative positions of an added pseudo-line with respect to a pseudoline system, with edges given by specialization/generalization arcs, and whose 2-cells are glued to give a surface.
ideas.modern_name: Extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid (pseudoline arrangement) / one-element extension poset as a cell complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Levi (1926, enlargement lemma); Las Vergnas; Sturmfels–Ziegler 1993 'Extension spaces of oriented matroids' (rank-3 extension space homotopy equivalent to a sphere); Mnëv–Ziegler

ideas.what: The 2-faces are squares whose four corners have the cyclic pattern spec→spec, gen→spec, gen→gen, spec→gen, and they are in bijection with pairs (relative position, incidence arc of specialization type), equivalently of generalization type.
ideas.modern_name: Square 2-cells of commuting elementary moves (cf. 2-cells of higher Bruhat orders / flip complexes of pseudoline arrangements)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Manin–Schechtman 1989; Ziegler 1993 (higher Bruhat orders); Ringel 1956 (flip connectivity)

ideas.what: Holes left by the hypercritical (multiply degenerate) positions are capped with polygonal disks glued along exceptional specialization arcs; a surface with boundary is encoded by a graph with free edges (fixed points of tau).
ideas.modern_name: Polygonal 2-cells for higher-codimension strata (Zamolodchikov-type relations; cellular strata of realization/extension spaces); ribbon-graph/carte encoding of surfaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Manin–Schechtman; Kapranov–Voevodsky (higher Bruhat as cellular); Grothendieck's own 'cartes' formalism (Esquisse 1984)
ideas.where_published: The graph/cartes formalism (S, A, sigma, tau) parallels the 'cartes' of Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the pseudo-line material is not published.

missed.claim: Grothendieck is building, by hand, a cellular model of the space of one-element extensions of a pseudoline arrangement and aiming to show it is a closed surface. This is essentially the rank-3 case of the extension space problem treated a decade later by Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993). He approaches it with the 'cartes' (sigma, tau) formalism contemporaneous with Esquisse d'un programme. Neither the oriented-matroid literature nor the Esquisse literature links the two.
missed.quote: La construction de la surface cellulaire n'est pas complète, car on a laissé de côté, dans le processus de recollement, les positions relatives hypercritiques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an independent, explicit cell structure (squares plus polygons for hypercritical strata) on the rank-3 extension space, with a combinatorial description of the 2-cells by pairs (L, a). It may give a direct proof that the extension space is a surface, rather than only a homotopy statement, and it connects pseudoline moduli to dessins/cartes.

missed.claim: The enumeration of square faces via critical digons plus a choice of contractibility arc and cotriangle is left open. The uniqueness of that choice ('a priori ... plusieurs') is not settled.
missed.quote: S'il y a un arc de contractibilité ayant un cotriangle au dessus de (S,t) ... et les choisir.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A clean bijective description of the 2-cells would give explicit Euler-characteristic counts for extension spaces of pseudoline arrangements.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a technical step, describing square faces and noting missing hypercritical cells, inside an unpublished, substantial project. That project amounts to a cellular construction of extension spaces of rank-3 oriented matroids predating Sturmfels–Ziegler, done in Grothendieck's cartes language. This page alone contains no completed new theorem.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'côté des' is written above the struck-out 'type'; read '1 côté des spécialisations (les arcs aboutissant(s) sont de spécialisation)'.
The parenthesis after the list of four corners likely reads '(Ceci parcouru dans un sens, ou dans l'autre)' rather than '(espace ... dans un sens...)'.
'et a un arc ... d'incidence': the image looks closer to 'd'inertie', which fits 'cas d'inertie' on the previous page.
Right column: 'au dessus de (S,t)' rather than '(S,L)'; also line a) on the left reads 'les paires (S,t) de digons de Σ (critiques fermés)' and b) 'Pour une telle donnée (S,t,L)'.
'(a priori, il est permis les gentes avec circuits...)' is doubtful. It plausibly reads '(a priori, il peut y en avoir plusieurs...)'.
